summary.text: CA9 is the candidate with the strongest and most robust convergent evidence. It is up in tumour at RNA (log2FC 6.312) and protein (log2FC 2.269), replicates in TCGA-KIRC (log2FC 9.712), survives extrapolation to a pure tumour (RNA log2FC at purity 1: 7.787), and is carried by RCC cells in two independent single-cell datasets (tumour-cell share 0.976 and 0.981). Girentuximab reached PHASE_3. It stays in the convergence top 10 in 0.894 of random re-weightings. It is not prognostic in TCGA (Cox padj 0.933) and is not a DepMap dependency, so it is a targeting and imaging handle rather than a functional vulnerability.

NNMT is the strongest dual target-and-biomarker candidate. It is tumour-up (RNA log2FC 4.67, protein log2FC 2.709), tumour-intrinsic (purity-1 log2FC 5.256), prognostic in TCGA (Cox log HR 0.301, padj 0.00479), and its protein increase replicates in the confirmatory DIA cohort (log2FC 4.776). RCC cells dominate its expression in both single-cell datasets. Literature calls it a prognostic biomarker and potential target, but it has no clinical drug, so the target call is a small-molecule hypothesis.

CD70 is a surface antigen where omics, literature and clinical programmes agree: tumour-up RNA (log2FC 4.464) and protein (log2FC 2.421), TCGA-KIRC replication (log2FC 7.09), a purity-1 log2FC of 4.278, and cusatuzumab at PHASE_2. It has the best ADC suitability among known targets (0.746). The caveat is new in this run: immune cells hold 0.654 of its tumour transcripts and one of two single-cell datasets places it mainly in T/NK cells, so tumour-cell restriction is not established.

Much of the overall convergence top 25 consists of proximal-tubule genes lost in tumour (ALDOB, SLC22A8, PIGR, UMOD, FABP1), and the biomarker profile is led by PSAT1, PCK1 and ALDH6A1. These are prognostic loss biomarkers, not targets. The established driver VHL is mechanism, and the actionable route is HIF-2alpha (EPAS1, belzutifan at APPROVAL). EPAS1 is the only gene with a selective DepMap signal, and in single-cell data its transcripts sit mainly in endothelium. No omics-convergent target is a selective dependency, and no candidate separates the IMmotion150 treatment arms.

omics.text: CPTAC tumour-vs-normal omics separate two groups. Up-regulated genes (CA9, CD70, NNMT, ENPP3, SCARB1, SLC16A3, HK2) are up at RNA and protein and replicate in TCGA-KIRC. They fit the hypoxia- and glycolysis-driven state that follows VHL loss. Down-regulated genes (PSAT1, PCK1, ALDH6A1, CA4) mark loss of normal tubule identity, replicate in TCGA-KIRC and are prognostic, with higher expression protective for PCK1, ALDH6A1 and CA4.

ALDH6A1 is down in tumour (RNA log2FC -3.399, protein log2FC -1.925) and sits on 14q, which is lost in 0.355 of tumours, with a positive copy-number-to-expression correlation (cis rho 0.525). Higher expression is protective (Cox log HR -0.554, padj 9.45e-12). The copy-number link gives it a plausible genomic cause for its loss.

FABP6 is up at RNA (log2FC 4.006) and protein (log2FC 1.921), replicates in TCGA-KIRC (log2FC 6.431), and sits on 5q, which is gained in 0.573 of tumours (cis rho 0.309). Copy gain is therefore a likely driver of the increase. It is a robust target-profile gene but has no literature in the corpus.

literature.text: Literature and data converge most clearly for CA9 (tumour-enriched, PET imaging proof of concept), CD70 (overexpressed in RCC, minimal in normal tissue, a proposed HIF target) and NNMT (prognostic and inhibitor evidence). SLC16A3 has one mechanistic paper describing lactate-driven immune evasion through GPR81. Most claims rest on single retrospective, bioinformatic or preclinical studies. SCARB1, ENPP3, HK2 and PSAT1 have no ccRCC literature relations in the corpus, so their ranks are data-driven.

PSAT1 is the clearest literature disagreement. The only relevant sentence in the corpus describes PSAT1 as positively enriched in oncogenic signalling and glycolysis, whereas CPTAC and TCGA show it down in ccRCC. The sentence's context (cohort or cancer type) was not verified, so the contradiction is unresolved.

SLC6A19 is a down-regulated, protective-type biomarker whose only literature support is one bioinformatics-plus-cell study reporting that it inhibits invasion and proliferation and links to fatty-acid metabolism. That makes it a tumour-suppressive marker, not a drug target.

external.text: EPAS1 (HIF-2alpha) is the established ccRCC target: belzutifan is at APPROVAL and its Open Targets association score is 0.4871. It is the only candidate with a selective DepMap signal (selectivity 0.3, 0.208 of ccRCC lines dependent, padj 0.061, not significant at 0.05). Its low expression-driven convergence rank, despite clinical validation, is the main disagreement between the data-driven ranking and clinical reality.

Open Targets and UniProt split the tumour-up candidates by modality. CA9, CD70 and ENPP3 are membrane proteins with antibody or ADC programmes (girentuximab PHASE_3, cusatuzumab PHASE_2, AGS-16C3F PHASE_2). SCARB1 and SLC16A3 have only predicted tractability, and NNMT has no drug. None of them shows a ccRCC dependency, so tractability rests on surface accessibility, not on tumour dependency. VHL has the top Open Targets ccRCC association and is mutated in 247 of 511 tumours, but it is a tumour suppressor and not directly druggable.

cells.text: CA9 is tumour-intrinsic at single-cell resolution: 54.7% of RCC cells express it and RCC cells carry 0.976 of tissue transcripts. Paired by donor, it is higher in tumour cells than in proximal tubule (log2FC 7.739, padj 0.0189). The attribution replicates in the second single-cell dataset (tumour-cell share 0.981, tumour vs tubule log2FC 8.522).
NNMT's tumour-cell attribution holds in both single-cell datasets: RCC is the dominant group, with tumour-cell shares of 0.97 and 0.948 and tumour vs proximal tubule log2FC of 9.132 and 5.573.

The cell attribution of CD70 and SLC16A3 does not replicate. In Li 2022 both are dominated by T/NK cells (tumour-cell shares 0.345 and 0.327), while in Zhang 2021 they are dominated by RCC cells (0.964 and 0.809). Their tumour increase is reproducible, but which cells carry it is unresolved, so they should not be called tumour-intrinsic on single-cell grounds.

Several familiar targets are not tumour-cell genes in this dataset. EPAS1 transcripts are mostly endothelial, with only a 0.051 share in RCC cells. CD74 is held by macrophages and dendritic cells, and CXCR4 by CD8 T cells (0.563 of transcripts). MET is mainly in RCC cells (0.935 of tumour transcripts).

spatial.text: In Visium sections RCC explains CA9 in situ (composition-corrected share 0.999). High-CA9 spots are surrounded by RCC (observed neighbour share 0.4757 vs expected 0.3654, padj 0.0017), with only slight macrophage enrichment (log2 enrichment 0.099). CA9 marks the tumour compartment in situ, consistent with its single-cell and purity profile. The Visium panel does not cover CD70.

structure.text: Molecular-glue-degrader (MGD) scores rank candidate sites and are not evidence that a degrader exists. CA9's best site scores 0.546 (126.8 A3, pocket pLDDT 90.3, one accessible lysine), its model mean pLDDT is 76.56 and the ligand-site recall is 0.5, which makes it a modest site.

Among the discovery candidates, RAB42 has a confident model (mean pLDDT 85.31) and a small best site (MGD score 0.5348, 37.4 A3) with no ligand-site validation. COL23A1's model is poor (mean pLDDT 58.91) and its best site scores 0.2342, so it is not glue-tractable. No structural analysis was available for CD70 or NNMT.

discovery.text: In the tumour track, COL23A1 is the leading first-in-class candidate (novelty 0.767). It has no clinical drug, RCC cells hold 0.881 of its tumour transcripts, it replicates in TCGA-KIRC (log2FC 5.829) and survives extrapolation to a pure tumour (4.88 at purity 1), and vital-organ expression is low (maximum 3 nTPM, heart muscle). It is a surface or secreted protein, so an antibody is the realistic modality. There is no survival or DepMap dependency evidence.

RAB42 is the second tumour-track candidate (novelty 0.705). RCC holds 0.627 of its tumour transcripts, it replicates in TCGA-KIRC (log2FC 4.371) and keeps 3.189 at purity 1, it has 2 ccRCC papers and no clinical drug, and its vital-organ maximum is 2.6 nTPM (lung). It is a hypothesis with no functional evidence.

The stroma track gives OLFML2A (fibroblast-carried, 0.647 of transcripts, 27.9 nTPM in colon) and JAG2 (endothelial, 0.487 of transcripts). The immune pool is mostly immune genes, and the purity check separates them. LILRB4 drops from TCGA log2FC 3.7 to 0.508 at purity 1, and GBP5 falls to 0.417, so both are infiltration-driven markers of macrophage or T-cell abundance. GAL3ST4 (macrophage, 0.972 of transcripts) keeps only 0.401 at purity 1. All discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses, none is a selective dependency, and their literature counts are by gene symbol.

validation.text: External replication and the purity check strengthen the tumour-up targets. CA9, CD70, NNMT, SCARB1, SLC16A3 and ENPP3 replicate in TCGA-KIRC and keep their fold change at purity 1, so their bulk signal is not infiltration. In contrast, FCGR3A, LILRB4 and GBP5 are weakened: their bulk increase follows immune infiltration. Prognosis strengthens NNMT and the tubule-loss biomarkers (PSAT1, PCK1, ALDH6A1, ALDOB, SLC22A8) but not CA9, CD70 or SCARB1.

The confirmatory DIA proteomics cohort replicates the protein calls for NNMT, SCARB1, PSAT1 and PCK1, with direction and significance in agreement and larger fold changes than discovery. PCK1 also replicates at 2 of 2 measured phosphosites, while PSAT1's one phosphosite does not. CA9 and CD70 could not be tested there (too few matched pairs), which is missing data, not a failed replication.

Somatic driver status and dependency point elsewhere. VHL is mutated in 247 of 511 tumours (frequency 0.483) and acts through loss of function and the HIF-2alpha axis. Selective DepMap dependency weakens every omics-convergent target, and EPAS1 is the only candidate with a selective signal, which is borderline. None of the top candidates is a kinase, so protein-adjusted kinase activity does not inform them.

robustness.text: Under 1000 random re-weightings the target profile is stable at the top. SCARB1, CA9, SLC16A3, CD70, NNMT, ENPP3 and FABP6 stay robustly in the target top 10, and SCARB1 and CA9 have the narrowest intervals. In the biomarker profile PSAT1, PCK1, SLC6A19 and PPP1R1A are robust. NNMT and ALDH6A1 are high on average but their biomarker intervals are wider. CA9 is the only gene robustly in the overall convergence top 10. The tubule-loss genes ALDOB and SLC22A8 rank high overall, but their position depends on weights that favour omics and prognosis.

SCARB1 is the most weight-robust target-profile call (p_top10 0.968, 90% rank interval 1 to 8), even though it has no ccRCC literature in the corpus and no clinical drug. Its position rests on tumour-intrinsic up-regulation (purity-1 log2FC 3.762), an Open Targets genetic association (0.519) and confirmatory protein replication.
PSAT1 is the most weight-robust biomarker call (biomarker p_top10 0.986, 90% rank interval 1 to 4). It ranks low overall because the overall score mixes in target streams.

treatment.text: In IMmotion150 no candidate passes correction and no gene separates the two main arms. Higher CD70 is associated with longer benefit on atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (log HR -0.383 per SD, padj 0.166), and CA9 shows a similar non-significant direction (log HR -0.112, padj 0.665). The arm differences are not significant (CD70 padj 0.927, CA9 padj 0.779). PCK1 is associated with earlier progression on the combination (log HR 0.22, padj 0.572). For NNMT only the 16-patient nivolumab trial was returned, which supports no claim.

subtypes.text: CA9 is the only profiled subgroup candidate: it is higher in PBRM1-mutant tumours at RNA (CPTAC +0.971, padj 0.014; TCGA +1.148) but not significantly at protein (padj 0.067), and it is lower in ccB than ccA. NNMT does not differ by VHL, PBRM1, BAP1 or SETD2 status or between ccA and ccB, so it is a pan-subtype marker. PSAT1 is higher in ccB than ccA at RNA and protein and higher in BAP1 mutants at RNA only. Because subtype differences in bulk tissue can reflect infiltration, these are leads, not subgroup indications.

adc.text: For antibody-drug conjugates or radioligands, CD70 has the highest suitability among known targets (0.746, rank 2 of 2017), but no vital-organ staining data. CA9 (0.647) and ENPP3 (0.578) act as clinical controls: CA9 stains strongly in stomach and ENPP3 in duodenum and kidney. SLC16A3 scores high (0.725) and has the best weakest-quarter tumour coverage (43.7 percent), but it spans the membrane 12 times with only 66 extracellular residues. SCARB1 (0.558) has sparse tumour-cell coverage (7.1 percent in the weakest quarter of donors) and strong adrenal staining. A score does not show that a conjugate would work.

immune.text: Immune profiling separates candidates that are immune-cell genes from tumour-cell genes. FCGR3A is almost entirely immune (0.999 of tumour transcripts, immune score correlation 0.795), so its tumour increase reflects infiltration and marks hot tumours. CD70 is partly immune (0.654 of transcripts, correlation with CD8 T cells 0.278), so it tracks infiltration as well as tumour cells. CXCR4 and CD74 are infiltrating-lymphocyte and antigen-presenting-cell genes, and act as microenvironment controls. CA9 and NNMT remain tumour-cell genes.

integration.text: Read together, the layers separate three groups. First, targets where omics, literature, external knowledge and cell context all converge: CA9, a tumour-intrinsic surface antigen with a clinical antibody, and NNMT, the strongest dual target and biomarker, although NNMT is undrugged. CD70 belongs here on omics, literature and clinical grounds, but its cell attribution is contested. Second, data-strong targets with little prior knowledge: SCARB1, SLC16A3, ENPP3 and FABP6. Third, biomarkers of tubule-identity loss: PSAT1, PCK1, ALDH6A1, ALDOB and SLC22A8. The disagreements are informative. EPAS1 is clinically validated but ranks low on expression and is endothelial in single-cell data. The absence of a DepMap dependency for the convergent targets means they suit antigen-directed modalities better than inhibitors.

targets.rationale: Rank 1 in convergence and 2 in the target profile (p_top10 0.941). It is tumour-up at RNA, protein and in TCGA-KIRC, carried by RCC cells in two single-cell datasets, RCC-surrounded in situ, and targeted by girentuximab (PHASE_3). It is not prognostic and not a dependency, so it is best used as an antibody, radioligand or imaging target.

Robust in the target profile (p_top10 0.88) and rank 6 in the biomarker profile. It is tumour-intrinsic (purity-1 log2FC 5.256), prognostic (Cox log HR 0.301), replicates in confirmatory proteomics and in a second single-cell dataset, and has literature support. Placed second because it is the only candidate that holds in every validation layer. As a cytoplasmic enzyme with no clinical drug, the target call is a small-molecule hypothesis.

Tumour-up (protein log2FC 2.421), purity-1 log2FC 4.278, robust in the target profile (p_top10 0.88), supported by ccRCC literature as a HIF-driven surface antigen, with cusatuzumab at PHASE_2 and the best ADC suitability among known targets (0.746). Moved below NNMT because immune cells hold 0.654 of its transcripts and its single-cell attribution does not replicate.

Top of the target profile (score 4.1314) and the most weight-robust target (p_top10 0.968). It is tumour-up and intrinsic, its protein increase replicates in the confirmatory cohort (log2FC 2.334), and it has an Open Targets genetic association. Placed below CA9, NNMT and CD70 because it has no ccRCC literature, no clinical drug and sparse tumour-cell coverage for an ADC.

Rank 1 of the biomarker profile (p_top10 0.986). It is down in tumour (RNA log2FC -3.867), replicates in TCGA-KIRC and in confirmatory proteomics (log2FC -3.946), is prognostic (Cox log HR 0.43, padj 5.66e-7) and is higher in ccB than ccA. It is an expression-loss biomarker, not a target, and one literature sentence disagrees on direction.

Tumour-up membrane enzyme (RNA log2FC 3.895, purity-1 log2FC 5.278), robust in the target profile (p_top10 0.823), with an ADC (AGS-16C3F) at PHASE_2. Strong kidney and duodenum staining is an on-target toxicity liability, the corpus has no literature on it and there is no dependency.

Rank 2 of the biomarker profile (p_top10 0.889). It is down at RNA (log2FC -4.424) and protein, its loss replicates in confirmatory proteomics (log2FC -4.819) including 2 of 2 phosphosites, and higher expression is protective (Cox log HR -0.415).

MCT4 lactate transporter, tumour-up (protein log2FC 2.279), purity-1 log2FC 3.821, robust in the target profile (p_top10 0.881), with one mechanistic paper on lactate-driven immune evasion. It has no clinical drug or dependency, its single-cell attribution is discordant, and its 12-pass topology favours a small molecule over a conjugate.
Biomarker profile rank 3 (p_top10 0.773). It is down in tumour, with copy-number-linked loss (cis rho 0.525) and the strongest prognostic value (Cox log HR -0.554).

Rank 2 overall. It is strongly down (RNA log2FC -7.028, -6.302 at purity 1), and lower expression predicts worse survival (Cox log HR -0.358). Placed lower because its signal reflects lost proximal-tubule identity and its biomarker-profile rank depends on the weights.

Included despite a low convergence rank because it is the approved ccRCC target (belzutifan) and the only candidate with a selective DepMap signal (selectivity 0.3, padj 0.061). In single-cell data its transcripts are mostly endothelial, which is a caveat on reading its bulk expression.

limitations.text: All discovery omics are bulk tumour-vs-normal comparisons. The ranking is associative, not causal, and protein fold changes are compressed by TMT ratios.
No omics-convergent target shows a selective DepMap dependency in ccRCC lines, so the targets are supported for antigen-directed modalities, not as functional vulnerabilities.
The literature corpus is small (about 320 ccRCC abstracts), and most gene-level claims rest on one or two, often bioinformatic, studies. Absence of literature is weak evidence of absence.
IMmotion150 associations come from arms of about 88 patients and none survives correction. For NNMT, SCARB1 and EPAS1 only the 16-patient nivolumab trial was available.
CA9 and CD70 could not be tested in the confirmatory proteomics cohort, and HK2, ENPP3 and SLC16A3 were not checked there in this run, so their protein replication is untested rather than negative.
Single-cell context comes from two cohorts with small proximal-tubule groups, and the two disagree on whether tumour cells or T/NK cells carry CD70 and SLC16A3. Visium does not cover CD70.
MGD scores rank structural sites and are not evidence that a degrader exists. Ligand-site validation was available only for CA9.
Discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses without dependency or functional evidence, and their literature counts are by gene symbol.
STRING interactions were not queried, and EPAS1 was not profiled in the ADC, immune or subtype layers.
